title: Bacterial Species-Specific Computational Optimization of Primer/probE Sets (B-SCOPE): A Snakemake Based Pipeline for Predicting qPCR Reagents for Sensitive and Species-Specific Detection of Bacterial Pathogens
content: Developing quantitative PCR (qPCR) primer and probe sets to detect and distinguish between closely-related bacterial organisms can be time consuming, costly, and difficult to scale when performed manually. The resulting reagents also require extensive experimental screening to validate primers that are both highly sensitive and species-specific. Here we report the development of the B-SCOPE: Bacterial Species-specific Computational Optimization of Primer/probE sets workflow. This is an automated computational workflow to streamline the prediction of high-performing candidate qPCR primer and probe sets to differentiate and potentially diagnose infectious pathogen species using all relevant, publicly available, high-quality whole genomes. All assembled genomes for multiple strains of a target bacterial species and all genomes from members of the same genus were collected and analyzed using a reusable and scalable Snakemake-based bioinformatics pipeline. Genomes are first annotated using Prokka, followed by pan-genome analysis with Roary to determine gene presence or absence across strains. The workflow then identifies genes that are present in at least 99% of the target species, and either absent or rare in all other species of the same genus. Polymorphic alleles within these candidate genes are extracted and aligned using MAFFT to generate multi-sequence alignments and identify taxon-conserved regions for primer annealing that have high specificity and sensitivity for the target taxon (i.e. species). The existing Primer3 program was subsequently used to design candidate primer and probe sets based on predicted thermodynamic properties and sequence conservation for these target regions. We then applied this workflow to a use case that predicts sensitive and specific qPCR reagents for the Lactobacillus acidophilus species compared to other members of the same genus. Overall, this workflow generates a ranked list of candidate genes and primer configurations, providing an efficient framework for developing sensitive and specific molecular diagnostics using a scalable big data approach to identify target taxa.
